summary: Temporary session handoff fails for SSH gateway due to missing/mismatched Okta device_id claim
description:
Issue summary:
Users attempting to open SSH sessions via the internal SSH gateway (bastion) intermittently receive a 403 / 'device claim missing' error when the SSO handoff occurs. This started after the Okta claim-normalizer rollout (mar 9) that normalizes device-related attributes in SAML/OIDC assertions. Impact: on-call engineers and support staff in prod-us-west cannot open new SSH sessions via the console; existing sessions are unaffected.

Impact:
- Affected: internal-bastion access flow for ~15% of users in us-west over last 24h; primarily users with managed devices enrolled in Okta Device Trust.
- Severity: blocks elevated troubleshooting and runbook execution; classified Sev1 for operational impact.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-west
- auth stack: identity-proxy v1.9.2, ssh-gateway v2.3.0, okta-claim-normalizer v1.1.0 (rolled out mar 9), identity-service v3.4.1

Observed behavior:
- When clicking 'Open SSH session' from the console, the session creation popup fails with 'Authorization failed: missing device_id claim'.
- auth-proxy logs show: "token validation failed: device_id claim absent or mismatched" for affected tokens.
- Okta SAML assertion samples (redacted) show deviceId attribute present in some users but claim key normalized to "device_urn" by the claim-normalizer; downstream services expect "device_id".

Expected behavior:
- Device claim should be normalized consistently across the stack so that the auth-proxy and ssh-gateway accept the assertion and allow session handoff.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to console with Okta SSO for a managed device user in prod-us-west.
2) Navigate to 'Infrastructure' > 'SSH Gateway' and attempt to 'Open SSH session' to any host.
3) Observe the session creation failure and 403 in the UI.
4) Capture auth-proxy logs and inspect incoming assertion payload near the time of the attempt.
logs: 2026-03-13T18:12:04Z identity-proxy ERROR token validation failed: device_id claim absent or mismatched (user: u-xxxx)
2026-03-13T18:12:04Z ssh-gateway WARN session handoff aborted: device claim mismatch
Audit event: user u-xxxx attempted SSH handoff, auth-proxy rejected assertion (reason=claim_key_mismatch)
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:30 - Triage: Pattern shows users with Okta-managed devices are affected; unmanaged user logins succeed.
03/10 11:00 - Reproduced in staging by simulating Okta assertion where device claim key is 'device_urn' instead of 'device_id'. auth-proxy fails validation.
03/11 14:20 - Correlated start time with okta-claim-normalizer v1.1.0 rollout (mar 9). That service started normalizing device attributes to 'device_urn' to match an internal naming initiative.
03/12 08:45 - Identity team confirms claim-normalizer was rolled without updating downstream consumers. Affected consumers include auth-proxy and ssh-gateway which still expect 'device_id'.
03/13 10:10 - Quick test: adding a compatibility mapping in identity-proxy (accept device_urn as device_id) resolves the handoff in a local repro environment.
03/13 16:05 - Security review: device claim content is same (unique device identifier), only the attribute key changed. No evidence of tampering.
Hypothesis: claim-normalizer inadvertently renamed the attribute key but did not provide feature flagging for downstream migration.
comments: Priya Shah (Reporter) 2026-03-10: User Derek J. reported inability to open SSH sessions; attached screenshot and time window. Escalating to Identity on-call.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) 2026-03-10: I will reproduce in staging and check recent Okta-related rollouts. Assigning to identity team for claim mapping check.
Nina Gupta (Identity) 2026-03-11: Found claim-normalizer change introduced on Mar 9. We're preparing a compatibility fix to emit both 'device_urn' and 'device_id' for a window.

SRE on-call (Marco Ruiz) 2026-03-13: Deployed a temporary config to identity-proxy to accept 'device_urn' as alias for 'device_id' in us-west; initial telemetry shows success rate of SSH handoffs improved from ~85% to ~99% for affected users.
Security (Ayesha Patel) 2026-03-13: Confirmed no change to device identifiers themselves; approve compatibility window approach. Need rollback plan and audit entries for changes.
Liam O'Connor 2026-03-14: Preparing hotfix PR to identity-proxy to support both keys and updating ssh-gateway to tolerate either key. Targeting 2026-03-14 20:00 PDT deployment.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: identity-proxy configuration updated to accept 'device_urn' as an alias to 'device_id' in prod-us-west (mar 13 16:05). This restored SSH handoff for affected users. Work items: 1) merge and deploy hotfix that adds backward-compatible key handling across identity-proxy and ssh-gateway (PR created). 2) Coordinate with identity/Okta team to update claim-normalizer to emit both keys during migration window, then converge on canonical key. 3) Add automated integration test to catch attribute-key drift in CI. Post-incident: runbook update to include claim key mapping checks before Okta claim-rollouts.

Add integration test in identity-proxy CI validating incoming SAML/OIDC attribute keys (owner: Liam O'Connor) - due 2026-03-18
Update SSH Gateway runbook to include explicit claim keys expected and fallback mappings (owner: SRE) - due 2026-03-22
